solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unacceptable behaviour of naughty pupils (3,4)

blocks.note: the idiom for conduct that breaks unwritten social rules
naughty = bad, and pupils make up a school class

explanation.surface: A teacher's verdict on a class that has been misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a class is called a form (the fifth form), which is what makes naughty pupils a BAD FORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad form is the idiom for behaviour that breaks unwritten social rules.

clue.text: Wound some quiet Iberians up (4)

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used
in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: quiET IBerians holds ETIB, read upwards

explanation.surface: Someone has riled a group of quiet Spaniards and Portuguese.
explanation.walkthrough: Wound looks like the past tense of wind (as in wound up), but here it is the noun: an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an animal's or insect's bite is the injury it leaves.

clue.text: One conscripted after cycling into Delaware (7)

indicators.note: the letters go round like a wheel: the last one comes to the front
the result goes inside the abbreviation

blocks.note: DE is the postal abbreviation for the US state
AFTER with its last letter R moved to the front

explanation.surface: A man called up for service is sent on to Delaware after a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a cyclist, but cycling is an instruction: rotate AFTER to RAFTE, then put it inside D…E.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is someone drafted, the American word for conscripted.

clue.text: Building work is on time (5)

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sitting on another is placed above it

blocks.note: op = opus, a numbered musical work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A builder's claim that a construction job is keeping to schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Building work reads as one phrase about construction; split it, and Building is the definition while work is OP. The Opera is also the name of the building, as in the Paris Opéra.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is the house where opera is performed, like the Paris Opéra or the Sydney Opera.

clue.text: Gathers wrong military intelligence on cutters (8)

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits on top of the second

blocks.note: the initials of Military Intelligence, as in MI5
shears are large cutting blades

explanation.surface: Spies collect faulty intelligence about people who cut things.
explanation.walkthrough: Gathers here means understands (I gather you're leaving), so gathers wrong is to hear wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mishear is to gather the wrong meaning from what was said.

clue.text: Builder of bridges in hostel for dossers (7)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: hosTEL FOR Dossers

explanation.surface: A builder of bridges is found sleeping in a hostel for the homeless.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Telford was a Scottish engineer famous for his bridges and canals. A dosser is British slang for a homeless person.
explanation.definitionFit: Telford built the Menai Suspension Bridge and many others.

clue.text: Gift of story books (6)

blocks.note: a tale is a story
NT = New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A book of stories given as a present.
explanation.walkthrough: Gift looks like a present, but it is a natural ability. Books is often OT or NT in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a natural ability, as in a gift for music.

clue.text: Mocked and hit setter in school (9)

indicators.note: the setter's word goes inside the school

blocks.note: to lam is to thrash
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
the setter can refer to themselves as one

explanation.surface: A pupil was teased and beaten by a setter at school.
explanation.walkthrough: School is a group of whales here, not a place of learning, and setters often call themselves one.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon is to mock through satire.

clue.text: Not a member of away team (7)

definitions.note: Outside is a preposition here, standing for the whole phrase not a member of.

blocks.note: away and out both mean not at home
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A player who is not part of the visiting team.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on into of, so it reads as not a member of the away team; the split comes after of.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition covers the whole phrase: to be outside the club is to be excluded from it.

clue.text: Injurious to reputation of someone brilliant and loving (10)

blocks.note: def is slang for excellent
amatory means relating to love

explanation.surface: Gossip damages the name of someone gifted and affectionate.
explanation.walkthrough: Def, from hip-hop slang, means brilliant or cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Defamatory statements damage someone's good name.

clue.text: Crossing middle of hall, led by tango dancers (9)

indicators.note: take the central letters of the next word
the other pieces come before it

blocks.note: T is tango in the NATO alphabet
ravers dance at raves
the central letters of hALl

explanation.surface: Tango dancers cross the middle of a dance hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango and hall make it all look like ballroom dancing; tango gives just its NATO letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from traverse, to go across a mountain face or a room.

clue.text: Second pet clipped in repeated pattern (5)

indicators.note: a clipped word has its end cut off

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second (half a mo)
a pet is a fit of sulking, a tiff; clipped loses its last F

explanation.surface: A second pet has been trimmed into a repeating design, like topiary.
explanation.walkthrough: Pet is not an animal but a sulk (to be in a pet), which gives TIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a design or theme that recurs in a pattern.

clue.text: Workers’ movement wasted inordinate sum (5,8)

indicators.note: wasted means ruined, so the letters are wrecked

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

explanation.surface: A labour movement squandered a vast amount of money.
explanation.walkthrough: Movement looks like a physical action; it is a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Movement in its political sense: organised labour campaigning through unions.

clue.text: Indigestion remedy averts ills abroad (5,5)

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are spread about

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A stomach remedy that heads off sickness on foreign holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a travel health tip; abroad is only an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Liver salts are a fizzy mineral powder taken for indigestion.

clue.text: Regularly spurned fiancé’s kiss, bold and clumsy (8)

indicators.note: every other letter is rejected, starting with the first

blocks.note: fIaNcE with F, A and C thrown out
X is a kiss at the end of a letter
pert = cheeky, bold

explanation.surface: A jilted fiancé's kiss was forward and awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurned fiancé suggests an ex, but spurned works on the letters: the odd ones go.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexpert means lacking skill, so clumsy.

clue.text: Quietly point out dodgy financial contract (3,6)

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound, so the letters are unreliable

blocks.note: p = piano, quietly in music
anagram of POINT OUT, 8 letters

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly flags up a suspicious money deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Dodgy seems to describe the contract, but it acts on point out.
explanation.definitionFit: A put option is a contract giving the right to sell an asset at a set price.

clue.text: Cases of urban resistance suggest trouble (6)

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so take each word's first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of UrbaN
the first and last letters of ResistancE
the first and last letters of SuggesT

explanation.surface: Instances of city rioting point to deeper trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Suggest looks like the link word; it is the third word whose cases are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, in the sense of civil disturbance: trouble on the streets.

clue.text: Hunting of cheetahs condemned (3,5)

indicators.note: condemned means doomed, so the letters are broken up

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: The hunting of cheetahs has been denounced.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheetahs hunt by chasing, so the fodder already belongs in the answer's picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The chase is an old name for hunting as a sport.

clue.text: Former leading lady posed with unknown substitute (6)

blocks.note: ER = Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen
to sit for a portrait is to pose
x, y and z are the unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: An old film star posed alongside an anonymous stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: Leading lady points to an actress, but it is the monarch: Elizabeth II, now former, was ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A German loanword used as an adjective or noun for a poor imitation, like ersatz coffee.

clue.text: Trophy wife fell at last for surgeon’s knife (7)

indicators.note: take the final letter of each of the two words

blocks.note: a scalp is a trophy of victory
the last letters of wifE and felL

explanation.surface: A trophy wife has fallen for a surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: Trophy wife is a set phrase that must be split: Trophy is SCALP, and wife gives only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is the small sharp knife used in surgery.

clue.text: Rabble crushing arthropod’s shell and tail (8)

indicators.note: the rabble squeezes around the other piece
the shell is the outside, so take the first and last letters

blocks.note: a shower is British slang for a useless bunch of people
the outer letters of ArthropoD

explanation.surface: A mob stamps on a crab's shell and tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Shell and tail both sound like parts of the arthropod; tail is really the definition, as in someone who tails a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail is a person who follows someone secretly, a shadower.

clue.text: Climbing tree, foul inside and full of beetles (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing reads the word upwards
the second piece goes into the first

blocks.note: YEW read upwards
foul and evil both mean wicked

explanation.surface: A rotten tree someone is climbing turns out to be crawling with beetles.
explanation.walkthrough: Foul inside reads like a description of the rotten tree; it is an instruction to put a word for foul into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Weevils are beetles, so something weevily is infested with them.

clue.text: Show resentment while supporting brother (6)

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting piece goes underneath

blocks.note: BR is an abbreviation for brother
to while away time is to idle it away

explanation.surface: Someone resents having to keep propping up a sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: While looks like a conjunction meaning during; it is the verb, as in while away the hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to show anger or resentment, like a horse throwing up its head.

clue.text: Chicanery in spades, with repeated string-pulling? (5,8)

blocks.note: S = spades in card games
a harp is played by plucking its strings
practice is doing something over and over

explanation.surface: Dishonest dealing in abundance, with plenty of pulling strings behind the scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: In spades means in abundance, and string-pulling means using influence; read literally they give S and a harpist's repeated plucking, HARP PRACTICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp practice is dishonest but barely legal dealing, which is chicanery.

clue.text: Idealised representation of Shakespearean villain gripping millions (5)

indicators.note: the villain holds the other letter inside him

blocks.note: Iago is the schemer in Othello
M = million

explanation.surface: A portrait of Iago that flatters him, holding millions.
explanation.walkthrough: Imago is a term from psychoanalysis for an idealised mental image of a person, usually a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is an idealised image of someone formed in the unconscious.

clue.text: Movie stars both turned out to be trouble (4)

indicators.note: both words have their insides thrown out, leaving only their outer letters

blocks.note: MoviE
StarS

explanation.surface: Two film stars went bad and caused a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Turned out looks like the phrase meaning proved to be; here it empties both words of their middles.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a predicament: getting into a scrape means landing yourself in difficulty.

clue.text: Audibly slap Italian painter (5)

indicators.note: the answer is said like the word the clue gives

blocks.note: slap and lippy are British slang for make-up and lipstick

explanation.surface: A hard slap across the face of an Italian painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Slap is not a blow but British slang for make-up; lippy is slang for lipstick. Filippo Lippi was a Florentine Renaissance painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fra Filippo Lippi and his son Filippino were Italian painters.

clue.text: Doctor and a colleague checking one’s ready for theatre (9)

indicators.note: to check is to hold back, so the colleague holds the next piece

blocks.note: Dr = doctor
as printed
a mate is a work colleague
one is I, so one's (one is) is I'S

explanation.surface: A doctor and a fellow medic confirm a patient is prepared for the operating theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Theatre suggests surgery, but the definition is a verb: to ready a story for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready is a verb here: to prepare a novel or story as a stage play is to adapt it for theatre.

clue.text: Quiet because eating seconds of blancmange and jelly (7)

indicators.note: the outer word swallows the other letters
take the second letter of each word

blocks.note: since = because
bLancmange, jElly

explanation.surface: Someone falls silent while eating a dessert of blancmange and jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: Seconds suggests a second helping of pudding; here it means second letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Silence and quiet are both a verb and a noun meaning the absence of noise.

clue.text: Spy on me, travelling in Bolivia and Colombia? (7)

indicators.note: things that are travelling do not stay in one place, so the letters move to new positions

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: An agent is tailed on a trip through South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: Bolivia is named after Simón Bolívar and Colombia after Columbus.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym is a name taken from a person, as these two countries' names are.
